cf.title: doc: Mention that * does not include system columns

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The change rewrites one sentence on the SELECT reference page to state existing behaviour, and Peter Eisentraut's placement concern in message #3 was addressed by moving the text there. Confidence is medium because only the v1 hunk is shown, so the v4 wording cannot be checked.

brief.title: Doc: say that * in the select list excludes system columns
brief.problem: A doc comment on the lexical syntax page asked to tell readers that * does not return system columns such as ctid. It suggested the example `SELECT ctid, * FROM t;` and a link to the System Columns section. The audience is SQL users reading the docs.
brief.proposed_design: v1 added a sentence, an example and a link to the asterisk item in section 4.1.4. After Peter Eisentraut's review, v2 moved the change to the SELECT List section of the SELECT reference page. v4 rewrites the first sentence there to say * is a shorthand for all the columns of the selected rows, not including system columns, with a link to that section.
author_claims: The docs build cleanly with make check and make html for each version.
"not including system columns" fits the existing docs better than "user-defined columns", which the docs do not use for this.
An endterm with free text fails the doc check, so v4 uses a link element that renders the same text.
brief.thread_state: Peter Eisentraut moved the change to the SELECT reference page and did not reply after that. Matemática A3K shaped the v3 and v4 wording and gave a +1 on v4; no committer has commented on v4.
unclear: Only the v1 hunk is shown, so the exact v4 text and its place on the SELECT reference page cannot be checked.
The patch does not say whether table_name.* is covered by the v4 wording; v2 named it but v3 rewrote that text.
Nobody says whether other pages that describe * expansion, such as composite types or row constructors, need the same note.
search_queries: asterisk does not include system columns

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the v4 sentence on the SELECT reference page also cover table_name.*, which v2 named and v3 rewrote?
Do other pages that describe * expansion, such as composite types or row constructors, need the same note or a link to this one?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut reviewed v1 in message #3 and chose the target page, but has not commented on v4; a committer who handles documentation would sign it.
committability.liability: One sentence and one link on the SELECT reference page; the owner signs for the wording being accurate and the link target staying valid.
committability.author_follow_up: The author revised the patch from v1 to v4 in response to review, which suggests continued follow-up.

priority.reason: A reader asked for this through the docs comment form (message #1), and the change is one sentence plus a link on one page. A reviewer gave +1 on v4; it needs a committer to read the final wording.

provisional_note: Only the v1 hunk for syntax.sgml is shown. The v4 text, its exact place on the SELECT reference page, and whether it covers table_name.* could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_stat_statements: add last_execution_start column
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a last_execution_start column to pg_stat_statements, which records the statement start timestamp of the most recent execution of each entry. Later versions store the timestamp in EState at ExecutorStart, so that ExecutorEnd, which the extended query protocol defers to the next execution, still records the right time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund opposed adding any more work under the pg_stat_statements spinlock, because pgss contention already brings instances down, and asked for the pgss design to be fixed first. Sami Imseih agreed that the column should wait for the pg_stat_statements redesign discussed in another thread. The author accepted this and planned to rebase on that work later, then withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
FWIW, I remain opposed to adding *any* additional thing under the spinlock. We
first need to fix the design of pgss, then we can start discussing expanding
it even further.

precedents_retrieved.title: document the hook system
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Tom Lane, Bruce Momjian
precedents_retrieved.summary: David Fetter proposed a WIP patch that adds a section on the hook system to the Postgres documentation. The goal was to make the existence and use of hooks discoverable without reading the source code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut found the patch too incomplete to evaluate, and it was closed after no new version was posted. Tom Lane argued that detailed, stable hook documentation would go out of date and discourage new hooks, so at most a short plain-text README should list them. Bruce Momjian agreed, and the thread reached no agreement on whether to use SGML documentation or a README.

This reverts commit 083d29c65b7897f90c70e6dc0a4240a5fa75c8f2.

precedents_retrieved.title: ALTER TABLE - check for column existence before starting operations
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a check in the first (preparation) pass of ALTER TABLE so that a column referenced by a subcommand such as SET NOT NULL is verified to exist, or to be added by another subcommand, before any expensive work like building a primary key starts. The goal is to fail fast on typos instead of holding a long lock and generating WAL that is then discarded.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The only review raised a memory-release issue (the heap tuple not being freed) and a behavioural regression: because subcommands run in passes by type, a command that alters a column and adds the same column later in the list used to succeed and fails with the patch, which could break backward compatibility. The visible messages show no revised patch or author reply after that review, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure how important it is. But I think it could break backward
compatibility.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Use Foreign Key relationships to infer multi-column join selectivity".
precedents_retrieved.authors: Simon Riggs, Tom Lane, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Use Foreign Key relationships to infer multi-column join selectivity".
Reverted commit(s): Use Foreign Key relationships to infer multi-column join selectivity; Load FK defs into relcache for use by planner; Clean up foreign-key caching code in planner.; Minimal fix for crash bug in quals_match_foreign_key.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts 137805f89 as well as the associated commits 015e88942,
5306df283, and 68d704edb.  We found multiple bugs in this feature, and
there was concern about possible planner slowdown (though to be fair,
exhibiting a very large slowdown proved difficult).  The way forward
requires a considerable rewrite, which may or may not be possible to
accomplish in time for beta2.  In my judgment reviewing the rewrite will
be easier to accomplish starting from a clean slate, so let's temporarily
revert what's there now.  This also leaves us in a safe state if it turns
out to be necessary to postpone the rewrite to the next development cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Using multicolumn statistics for more precise join selectivity estimatation
precedents_retrieved.objectors: vignesh C, Yugo NAGATA, Tomas Vondra
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch had two parts. One let the planner use extended (multicolumn) statistics, specifically functional dependencies, when estimating join selectivity. The other made auto_explain create multicolumn statistics automatically, or just suggest them, when a plan node's estimated row count differs from the actual count by more than a threshold.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last visible message (July 2021) reports that the patch no longer compiled on Windows against changed ModifyTableState fields. The same message says Yugo Nagata's open review comments still needed addressing, and the entry was moved to Waiting on Author. Those comments included duplicate statistics suggestions causing a unique-constraint error, redundant suggestions, and a request to explain why each statistic is suggested. Earlier, Tomas Vondra had suggested moving the advisor into a separate extension rather than auto_explain, collecting data across many runs, and not creating statistics automatically. The visible messages show no new version after that, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also Yugo Nagata's comments need to be addressed, I'm changing the
status to "Waiting for Author".

constraints, triggers, etc. are parallel-safe for the partition hierarchy

we could have used existing cached information in some cases like indexes,
domains, etc. to determine the parallel-safety.

precedents_retrieved.title: ALTER SYSTEM READ { ONLY | WRITE }
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER SYSTEM READ ONLY and ALTER SYSTEM READ WRITE, which stop or allow WAL writes cluster-wide without a restart, for controlled switchover and failover. The checkpointer emits a global barrier, sessions holding an XID are terminated, and the state is stored in the control file so it survives a restart.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They end with the author still reworking how StartupXLOG and the checkpointer run end-of-recovery steps, after review from Robert Haas, and noting that more work remained on the main patches.

precedents_retrieved.title: WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING Temporal Tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds SQL:2011 system-versioned temporal tables, keeping current and historical row versions in one table with generated row start and row end timestamp columns. Queries without a system time filter get an implicit filter for current rows, and FOR SYSTEM_TIME clauses query past data.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Vik Fearing, after trying to fix the patch, judged its design too flawed, because it conflates system_time periods with system versioning; ALTER TABLE ADD/DROP SYSTEM VERSIONING adding and removing columns was one example. Earlier review points such as the missing 2201H error for anomalies stayed open. Simon Riggs saw weeks of further work on one of two possible designs, had no plans to continue, and suggested Return with Feedback. The patch also no longer applied.
matched_queries: asterisk does not include system columns
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The design decisions are just too flawed, and it conflates system_time
periods with system versioning which is very wrong.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: System username in pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an authname column to pg_stat_activity that shows the externally authenticated user name, the same value the SYSTEM_USER keyword returns. It also covers methods such as peer and ident, which have no view of their own like pg_stat_gss.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stopped in February 2024 during an open discussion about whether pg_stat_activity already has too many columns and should be split into several views. Magnus Hagander replied that moving columns would break existing monitoring tools, and no one answered. Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback in October 2024 because nobody had posted since.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This is the last message sent on this thread, and an entry was still registered in the CF app, so I am marking that as RwF for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add parallel columns for seq scan and index scan on pg_stat_all_tables and _indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel_seq_scan, last_parallel_seq_scan, parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan columns to pg_stat_all_tables, and parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan to pg_stat_all_indexes. The goal is to help administrators judge how parallel workers are used and tune parallelism settings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers doubted that per-table and per-index counts of parallel scans help with tuning, since parallel plans with Gather nodes are usually analyzed per statement. Michael Paquier added that the metrics committed in e7a9496de906 and 5d4298e75f25 may already cover the need. Robert Haas found no clear use case for these counters. The author agreed that the committed metrics were good enough for now.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the question to which we don't have a clear answer is: for what purpose would you want to be able to distinguish parallel and non-parallel scans on a per-table basis?

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The precedent search returned no attempt with the same or a similar idea. The thread points to no earlier discussion of this doc change, so no earlier rejection reason applies.

The patch changes only one sentence of documentation and touches no syntax, GUC, catalog, dump format or client behaviour, so nothing in the standards and compatibility angle can break. It also states existing behaviour correctly: in Postgres, * leaves out system columns. One open point is wording: v4 is not shown, so it cannot be checked whether table_name.* is still covered. That is a docs-review question, not an objection.

The patch only changes documentation text on the SELECT reference page. It has no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or ABI change, so this angle has nothing to object to.

The patch changes one sentence of documentation about * and system columns. It grants nothing, exposes nothing and changes no defaults, so there is no privilege or exposure aspect to object to from the security angle.

No maintenance or fit objection. The v4 change rewrites one sentence on the SELECT reference page and adds a link. It adds nothing to code, the catalog, the hot path or the extension API. Peter Eisentraut steered the change to the page that is the authoritative source (message #3), so the fit concern was settled in the thread. Only the v1 hunk is shown, so the exact v4 text and whether it covers table_name.* could not be checked.

From this angle there is no concrete existing alternative to name. Peter Eisentraut said in message #3 that the SELECT reference page does not state this, and I cannot confirm that any other page says * excludes system columns, so there is no duplication to raise. A docs-only change also has no extension or hook alternative.

A user asked for this through the docs comment form (message #1), and a second reader called it useful (message #10). The change rewrites one sentence on the SELECT reference page, so maintenance cost is close to zero and it adds no user-visible surface beyond the doc text. That demand is enough for a doc clarification of this size, so the demand angle has no objection to raise.
